points.description: States that a queue is a data structure that stores elements following the first in, first out (FIFO) principle (first element added is the first removed).
points.partial_credit: Half or more of the marks for a vague or partly correct statement, e.g. says it is a data structure where items are removed in order of arrival without naming FIFO, or names FIFO without saying it is a data structure.

points.description: Names the main operations as enqueue (add) and dequeue (remove).
points.partial_credit: Half a mark if only one of the two operations is named correctly.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the core fact: a queue is a data structure that works on first in, first out, in any wording. The enqueue and dequeue operations are worth a smaller part; give part marks if only one is named. A wrong claim such as last in, first out (stack) loses P1, but does not affect P2. Answers that only talk about waiting in line or something unrelated get little or nothing.
